subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the title of OCR Component 02 in GCSE (9-1) English Literature (J352)?
options: Exploring modern and literary heritage texts
questions.explain: Component 02 (Paper 2) of J352 is titled 'Exploring poetry and Shakespeare'.

questions.q: How long is the OCR Paper 2 (Exploring poetry and Shakespeare) examination?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is a 2-hour written examination.

questions.q: What proportion of the overall GCSE does Paper 2 represent?
questions.explain: Paper 2 is worth 50% of the total GCSE marks.

questions.q: What is the total number of marks available on Paper 2?
questions.explain: Paper 2 carries 80 marks, split across the poetry and Shakespeare sections.

questions.q: What is the title of the OCR GCSE English Literature poetry anthology used for 'Poetry across time'?
questions.explain: OCR's set poetry anthology for J352 is 'Towards a World Unknown'.

questions.q: Which two thematic clusters make up the OCR poetry anthology?
options: 'Power and conflict' and 'Love through the ages'
questions.explain: The anthology is divided into the 'Love and relationships' and 'Conflict' clusters.

questions.q: Which of the following is a set Shakespeare play in the OCR J352 specification?
questions.explain: Macbeth is one of OCR's set plays; Hamlet, Othello and King Lear are not on the J352 list.

questions.q: 'Blank verse', the dominant form in Shakespeare's plays, is best described as:
questions.explain: Blank verse is unrhymed lines written in iambic pentameter.

questions.q: Which assessment objective focuses on analysing a writer's use of language, form and structure to create meaning?
questions.explain: AO2 rewards analysis of language, form and structure using relevant subject terminology.

questions.q: Which assessment objective rewards understanding of the contexts in which texts were written?
questions.explain: AO3 assesses understanding of the relationships between texts and their contexts.

questions.q: Which assessment objective covers a personal, critical response supported by well-chosen quotations?
questions.explain: AO1 rewards an informed personal response with textual references, including quotations.

questions.q: Which assessment objective is concerned with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar?
questions.explain: AO4 assesses technical accuracy, including spelling, punctuation and the range of vocabulary and sentence structures.

questions.q: To answer the 'Poetry across time' question successfully, learners must primarily:
options: Compare two poems, analysing how each presents its subject
Summarise the plot of one poem
Write about a single poem in isolation
Translate the poem into modern English
questions.explain: The poetry section is comparative, requiring analysis of how poems present their subjects.

questions.q: In a Shakespeare play, a soliloquy allows the audience to:
options: Hear a character's private thoughts while alone on stage
Watch two characters argue on stage
Hear a chorus summarise the events
questions.explain: A soliloquy is a speech in which a character, alone on stage, reveals inner thoughts to the audience.

questions.q: In the Shakespeare section, learners are expected to:
options: Explore a printed extract and connect it to the play as a whole
Write about the extract only, ignoring the rest of the play
Memorise and reproduce the whole scene
questions.explain: The extract-based question requires close analysis of the extract linked to the wider play.

questions.q: Why is contextual understanding (AO3) valuable when writing about Macbeth?
options: Jacobean beliefs about kingship and witchcraft can deepen interpretation of the play
It allows learners to ignore the language of the text
Context replaces the need for quotations
It is only relevant to the poetry section
questions.explain: Understanding contemporary beliefs enriches interpretation and earns AO3 marks.

questions.q: A student writes: 'The audience knows Duncan trusts Macbeth, yet we have already heard Macbeth plan his murder.' Which technique is being identified?
questions.explain: Dramatic irony occurs when the audience knows something a character on stage does not.

questions.q: A student writes: 'Both poems use natural imagery, but the first celebrates nature while the second uses it to convey grief.' This shows the student is:
options: Making a comparative analysis of the poets' methods
Listing facts about the poets' lives
questions.explain: Contrasting how each poem uses the same technique is effective comparative analysis (AO2).

questions.q: To gain AO3 marks in an answer on The Merchant of Venice, a student should best:
options: Relate the play to relevant contextual factors such as attitudes of Shakespeare's time
Count the number of lines in the extract
Focus only on modern film adaptations
questions.explain: AO3 rewards linking the text to relevant contextual factors of the period.

questions.q: A student's Shakespeare essay has strong ideas but frequent spelling and punctuation errors. Which assessment objective's marks are most affected?
questions.explain: AO4 assesses technical accuracy, so repeated errors reduce the AO4 marks.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) English Literature (J352) specification; Paper 2: Exploring Poetry and Shakespeare
